hypothesis: The daemon-lazyinit lane's disclosed opposite-direction gap: the TS DaemonSupervisor binds through a three-part pre-bind choreography - (1) a socket-path LEASE (proper-lockfile on the socket path: empty {path}.lock dir, stale 5000ms, mtime refresh 1000ms, acquire retries 600x25ms ~=15s, onCompromised callback; held from before everything to after the exit unlink), (2) a STARTUP FENCE wait (startup-fences/<sha256(socket)>.json pinning the dying predecessor's pid+processStartId, persisted from its verified hello, cleared when the pinned process is gone; 10s default in start(), 60s in the update coordinator), and (3) a SUPERVISOR-OWNERSHIP CLAIM (~/.prime/supervisor-owners registry: guard-locked candidate-dir rename, conflict = socketPath OR descriptorDir, live-conflict refusal, dead-owner reclaim, phase ladder starting->owner, plus a 5s/1s shutdown-admission lease that blocks ownership during any stop window) - while the rust port binds with a momentary cleanup-lock (pa-core LockDir, same {path}.lock protocol, 5s staleness, NO refresher, held only across the stale-unlink probe at boot and the one-shot exit unlink) plus a post-bind boot_reap. Neither direction had been audited for semantic equivalence. The lane's job: read both bind paths exactly at their pinned heads, build the edge-case matrix side by side, and deliver the per-edge verdict - honest 'equivalent, no action' or registered divergences with concrete failure scenarios; a real gap gets a TS-convergent fix-candidate design whose implementation rides a follow-up lane (no perf claim, no PR from this lane).

parity_notes:
THE TWO CHOREOGRAPHIES. TS (daemon-supervisor.ts start()): lease-acquire(852) -> fence-wait(855) -> ownership-claim(857, refusal: live same-socket/same-descriptorDir owner OR active shutdown admission; dead owners reclaimed) -> prepare-under-lease(865: live-listener refusal, non-socket refusal, 1s grace, identity-stable unlink) -> listen -> BIND-TIME identity(879) + chmod 0600 -> adoption -> updatePhase('owner')(926) -> ready. Exit: workers stopped -> listener closed -> identity-guarded unlink UNDER the lease (a compromised lease skips the unlink) -> lease release -> ownership release. The lease is the load-bearing difference: a LIFETIME exclusion with a 1s liveness heartbeat (mtime refresh), 5s staleness, and a compromise notification wired to self-fence + relinquish. RUST (supervisor.rs run()): prepare(385: absent-path early-return takes NO lock; quick can_connect refusal; momentary LockDir held only across the stale-unlink window) -> bind(386) -> restrict(394) -> signal drain(411) -> boot_reap(423, linux-only: kills same-socket leftover workers and wedged same-socket supervisors, pidfd-gated TERM(2s)->KILL->verify(1s)) -> adoption/serve(486) -> exit-unlink(487) with socket_identity(path) computed AT CLEANUP TIME (the guard is vacuous - D1).

THE EDGE-CASE MATRIX. E1 two daemons racing, cold path: TS serializes at the lease (loser blocks 15s then fails); RUST both prepares no-op and the bind itself arbitrates (loser fails fast: 250ms quick-refusal or bind EADDRINUSE). Both converge to exactly one server; through the CLI ensure path both CLIs end up on the winner. VERDICT EQUIVALENT (failure latency/message only). E2 stale socket file after a crash: both refuse a live listener, wait a 1s grace with identity gates, unlink under the same {path}.lock protocol with 5s stale-lock reclaim; RUST additionally reaps the crashed predecessor's descriptor-less leftover workers (a real TS hole: they hold runtime session leases forever and bounce opens with 'Session is already active'; TS adopts only descriptor-backed workers). VERDICT EQUIVALENT on the socket path + the sanctioned #289 reap divergence (documented in-tree). E3 crashed-owner cleanup: no exclusion survives a crash in either shape (TS's stale lease is auto-broken at 5s by the successor; rust holds nothing at runtime). EQUIVALENT. E4a graceful restart/handover: TS queues the successor at the lease through the whole stop (the predecessor's unlink precedes the release); RUST fails the successor fast while the old serves, and the exit-unlink window is lock-serialized on both sides (the old's one-shot acquire SKIPS on contention = the successor owns the path; the successor's prepare clears NotFound or unlinks the old's dead-listening file under the lock). EQUIVALENT. E4b replaced-socket exit cleanup: TS captures the identity at listen (daemon-supervisor.ts:879, daemon-mode.ts:718) and compares it at exit, so a socket file REPLACED under the daemon is never unlinked by the old owner; RUST passes socket_identity(path) read at cleanup time at all three sites (supervisor.rs:487-490, worker.rs:813-816, supervisor_lost.rs:129-132) - the guard compares a fresh read with itself and is VACUOUS: the exit unlink removes whatever file is at the path, including a successor's live socket. REGISTERED DIVERGENCE D1 (real correctness gap). Concrete scenarios: (worker, most reachable) a force-stopped worker survives (D-state) past the supervisor's stop verdict, the supervisor relaunches its replacement on the SAME deterministic path (supervision.rs:416 reuses descriptor.socket_path -> worker-<hash12(supervisor sock)>-<id[:12]>.sock), the replacement binds, the old process later wakes and exits via exit_orphaned/exit_after_close -> the vacuous cleanup unlinks the REPLACEMENT's live socket -> routes to the replacement fail -> failure loop/session bounce until the next relaunch cycle; (supervisor) the socket file is removed externally (systemd-tmpfiles /tmp age rules; the TS module's own comment names macOS dirhelper's 3-day $TMPDIR sweep) and a successor binds while the original still serves its nameless listener -> the original's exit unlinks the successor's LIVE socket -> every new connect fails ENOENT while existing connections drain. TS makes the edge unreachable twice (lease blocks the successor; bind-time identity guards the unlink); rust has neither. E4c CORRECTION (2026-10-03, D2 lease follow-up): the claimed TS self-heal of a wedged-but-still-kernel-connectable listener is FALSE. After the 5s lease goes stale, a successor may acquire the lock but `prepareUnixDaemonSocketPath` still calls `canConnect(path, 250)` at daemon-socket.ts:149-151 pre-grace and :170-171 in-grace and rejects the live listener as already in use. The original remains wedged until it resumes/fences or is killed. The genuine D2 gap is lifetime EXCLUSION: when an external process renames the original serving socket pathname away while its supervisor remains live, Rust's short-lived lock allows a second supervisor to bind the vacated name; TS's 1s-refreshed supervisor-held lease makes the rival wait. TS lease acquisition/refresh/compromise: daemon-socket.ts:77-102; acquisition before prepare/bind: daemon-supervisor.ts:846-879; compromise fence: daemon-supervisor.ts:7379-7405; release on shutdown: daemon-supervisor.ts:7491-7500. Rust baseline VM failing-first gate gate_1791025001_2635548 at 33113a987: 2 D2 e2e failures, including `live_supervisor_lease_prevents_rebind_after_external_socket_rename`; fmt/clippy pass. E4d third-party successor during a stop window: TS's shutdown admission (5s lease, renewed across the whole stop; consumers: the update coordinator and shutdown --all) makes ownership acquisition refuse with daemon_shutdown_in_progress, and the startup fence makes ANY successor wait for the pinned predecessor process to exit (60s coordinator timeout); RUST has neither - only the coordinator's OWN successor is protected by its local fence-free wait_for_exit (pid+start-id poll, 30s budget), and a third-party daemon spawned in the window takes the socket the moment the old listener drops (the rust stop pass keeps the listener up until every worker stop settles, so the takeover can only begin in the predecessor's final exit microseconds - no mid-drain kill, no corruption), then the coordinator's own successor fails to bind and the update fails HONESTLY. REGISTERED DIVERGENCE D3 (availability/ordering gap: TS determinism 'the coordinator's successor always wins' is lost). E5 the boot_reap window vs the TS fence window: complementary, non-equivalent mechanisms. The TS fence window [persisted fence, pinned process exit] makes successors WAIT (never kill); the rust reap window [bind, first client/adoption] makes the successor CLEAN (kill leftovers). The reap covers the dead-predecessor leftover-lease edge (a genuine TS hole; linux-only elsewhere, the worker-side refused-registration self-heal substitutes - documented); the fence covers the dying-predecessor edge that D3 leaves open. DIVERGENT BY DESIGN (registered both ways; the reap is the sanctioned #289 divergence). E6 external socket-file unlink while serving: TS fail-closes (the lease blocks any successor; the original stays deaf to NEW clients until it exits; no split-brain). RUST: a successor binds immediately (prepare's absent-path early return probes nothing, locks nothing) -> two supervisors alive (linux: the successor's reap kills the original -> convergence; non-linux: split-serve until the 5-minute supervisor-lost window self-heals the workers or the operator acts), and when the original exits, D1 compounds: its vacuous exit unlink removes the successor's live socket. DIVERGENT BEHAVIOR (compound with D1): still exactly one path-holder at any instant (no corruption), but rust's convergence is linux-only and D1 can deafen the successor at the original's exit. E7 two daemons, same descriptor dir, different sockets: TS refuses (the OR-arm of ownerConflicts); RUST's descriptor dirs are keyed per socket path, so the arm is unreachable by construction. EQUIVALENT BY CONSTRUCTION. E8 bind-failure cleanup: TS releases lease + ownership on any startup failure and leaves descriptor-dir + config artifacts; RUST propagates out of run() with the momentary lock dropped, and persists the supervisor config BEFORE the bind (TS after the claim) - same net artifacts (cosmetic ordering). NIT: the deaf-give-up exit (accept_loop's 60-failure budget) returns Err through '?' BEFORE the cleanup call, leaving the socket file for the next boot's prepare (self-healing; TS's process-exit hook would have unlinked). E9 fence-record crash: TS self-cleans at the next boot (a dead pinned pid clears the record under the guard); rust has no fence records. VACUOUSLY EQUIVALENT. E10 hello/owner identity validation (consumer side): TS hello carries the durable generation + owner token; workers claim the generation and re-validate it against the registry on a poll (checkSupervisorFences -> assertDaemonSupervisorOwnerCurrent; ownership lost -> claim revoked, connection ended); the coordinator's validateReplacementDaemon refuses a 'successor' still carrying the predecessor identity. RUST hello: supervisor_generation = sup:<pid> and supervisor_owner_token = a FRESH UUID PER CONNECTION (supervisor/clients.rs:95-97) - wire-shape parity with no durable backing; the worker hello sets supervisor_generation: None; no fence check; no successor-vs-predecessor comparison (the wait-for-exit-then-spawn ordering substitutes). REGISTERED (consumer-side, medium): the registry-backed validation surface is unported (the rust daemon-discovery module doc already records the registry as 'not ported yet ... until the registry lane lands'); impact: a worker whose supervisor lost ownership keeps serving until connectivity fades (the 5-minute supervisor-lost window) rather than revoking at the registry's authority.

THE VERDICT: NOT equivalent. 6 edges equivalent (E1, E2, E3, E4a, E7, E8/E9 with one logged nit), three registered divergences with concrete failure scenarios (D1 correctness - the vacuous identity guard; D2 liveness - no holder heartbeat/wedge relinquish; D3 availability - no shutdown admission / startup fence for third-party successors), plus the deliberate in-tree-registered divergences (the #289 boot_reap closing a real TS hole in the TS->rust direction; the fence-free coordinator wait). The gap is NARROWED by the 2026-10-03 E4c correction above: TS does NOT self-heal a still-connectable wedged listener; its lifetime lease does exclude a rival after an external socket-path rename. D1 and D3 remain independently scoped, and the rust cleanup-lock+boot_reap shape covers a different edge set.

THE FIX-CANDIDATE DESIGN (TS-convergent choreography; implementation rides a follow-up lane, not this one). FIX D1 (small, frozen-surface-safe, highest value): capture bound_identity: Option<SocketIdentity> immediately after bind_transport (before restrict) in supervisor.rs run() and in the worker's connection bind; store it on Supervisor/Worker; pass the STORED value to all three cleanup call sites. This restores TS's replaced-socket guard 1:1 (TS daemon-supervisor.ts:879 -> :895, daemon-mode.ts:718 -> :1078-1080). No wire/TUI surface is touched; the socket.rs oracles already model the bind-time shape (cleanup_is_deferred_while_a_rival_holds_the_lock passes a bind-time identity; unlink_refuses_a_replaced_file_with_a_new_identity exists for the stale probe) - the follow-up lane adds the served-path replacement-rejection oracles at the three call sites (the window_serves pattern: assert the cleanup actually refused a differing identity, not vacuous equality). FIX D2 (design-registered; heavier): port the lease shape onto the cleanup lock - hold {path}.lock for the daemon's lifetime with a 1s mtime refresh (LockDir needs a refresh arm; proper-lockfile's update:1000 semantics), stale 5s; on refresh failure (the dir was reclaimed = a successor judged us gone) fence the supervisor socket (close listener, destroy client connections), SKIP the socket unlink (the TS compromised-lease guard), and exit. This gives the wedged-holder self-relinquish and the crash-takeover the same 5s bound TS has. FIX D3 (design-registered; needs the durable registry the rust discovery doc anticipates): port startup-fences/<sha256(socket)>.json (persisted from the stopping daemon's verified identity; waited at supervisor start; cleared when the pinned pid+start-id is dead) and the shutdown-admission lease (5s/1s; renewed by the update coordinator and shutdown --all; checked at ownership acquisition) - the rust registry dir can mirror ~/.prime/supervisor-owners. E10 rides the same registry lane (durable generation + owner token in the hello, the worker claim-validation poll, validateReplacementDaemon). Assumptions carried to the follow-up lane: (a) LockDir stays proper-lockfile-byte-compatible - a refreshed lifetime hold changes no other user (per-file locks, disjoint paths); (b) the #289 reap divergence STANDS (the fence complements, never replaces, the reap); (c) constants: TS lease stale 5000ms/update 1000ms/retries 600x25ms, fence poll 250ms/timeout 10s (supervisor) and 60s (coordinator), admission 5000ms/1000ms/50ms-wait; rust lock stale 5s/retries 600x25ms, predecessor-exit budget 30s, TERM grace 2s, KILL verify 1s, STOP_FORCE_TIMEOUT 10s.
